summary: Wrote src/en/module_02/30-exercises.md: the Exercises section (#exercises) with an introduction (grading, 130 minutes, collapsed solutions, a table mapping exercises to sections) and all 15 exercises e1-e15 in plan order (8 one-star, 6 two-star, 1 three-star, 130 minutes), each followed by a complete solution. Every number was computed in the lab environment with labpy.sh; coding solutions (e2, e4, e5, e6, e7, e8, e10, e11, e12, e15) are complete code that was run, with real output pasted in. check.mjs --module 2 --lang en reports 0 errors.
changes: e5(b): measured with Lab 1's seed: W1[0,5] = 0.10894 and the unit's gradients are exactly 0.0 as planned, but the run ends with 2 never-active units (unit 5 plus one that dies during training), not '63 other units still reach 2.8e-4'. Final training MSE 2.81e-4, validation 3.68e-4. The solution also freezes the unit's outgoing weight W2[5].

e7(d): the plan's 44 steps for heavy ball is measured against the initial norm; with the same measure gradient descent needs 216 (not 227, which is theta_1 alone), so the real speed-up from (1,1) is about 5 rather than the asymptotic 8. Both coordinates, not only the flat one, sit on a double root at the optimum. Both momentum forms are now defined in the prompt, and the Nesterov limit 2(1+mu)/((1+2mu)lambda_max) = 0.0212 is derived with the Jury conditions and simulated.

e12(c): the plan's solution said the loss's own gradient stays bounded away from zero because of the floor and that gradients shrink as the network becomes confident. That is not right as stated: the correct loss's gradient also vanishes for confident correct examples (the double-softmax and correct gradient norms are 2.7e-3 and 3.2e-3 at logit gap 8). The real mechanism, measured, is that the Jacobian diag(q) - qq^T tends to 0 at any one-hot q, so a confidently WRONG example gets gradient norm 8.7e-4 instead of 1.41 (more than 1000 times smaller). The prompt of (c) now asks which examples receive almost no gradient, and the solution has a table. The loss floor bound e/(e+K-1) is proved with Jensen's inequality, with floors 0.313, 1.461, 3.622, 5.909 for K = 2, 10, 100, 1000.

e13: the prompt's numbers did not match Lab 1. (a) at eps = 1e-11 Lab 1's errors are about 1e-5 typically and up to 3e-2 (not 1e-7 to 1e-4); (b) 'below 1e-9 everywhere' became 'below 1e-7' (Lab 1 has 5e-9 and 1.3e-8 on healthy tensors); (c) 'below 1e-8' for the second layer became 'below 1e-7'. In (c) the measured error range with the gate dropped is 0.29 to 1.00, consistent with the planned 0.2 to 1.

e10(c): dropped the plan's '92-93% against 96.7%' (Lab 5's outputs are predictions that will be replaced); the solution says 'a few points below' and points to Lab 5 script D. Added a million-draw simulation of the mean (2.501) and variance (4.166 against theory 4.167) of inverted dropout at p = 0.4.
e14(b): removed the plan's reference to 'Figure 2.21 (b)' (Section 14 is not written yet, so the panel is unknown); the solution cites the Section 14 'falls, then spikes' pattern instead.

e15: all plan numbers reproduced (SGD best eta 0.1, MSE 1.14e-4; Adam best 3e-3, 1.37e-6, 83 times lower; millimetres: SGD nan from 1e-6 and stuck at 0.1657 for eta <= 1e-7, Adam best 0.080 at eta 0.1). Added what the plan only asserted: eta = 0.3 raises the loss to 43 in three steps and leaves one live unit (0.127); the stuck value 0.1657 is exactly the best two-piece fit with kinks at 0 (least squares in the code); a block (b') showing that dividing W1 by 1,000 at initialisation (initial loss 0.327) does not rescue SGD (stable only to 1e-5, stuck at 0.165) and Adam only reaches 2.8e-3; and a finer SGD point in (c) (eta 0.06 gives 9.6e-5; the factor-3 grid alone shows 2.5e-3 at 0.03). The whole script runs in about 10 s, not the plan's 20 s.

e2(d), e4, e8, e11: all plan numbers verified unchanged (ratio 1.2533 for 784-256-256-10 and 1.683 for the digits network; f = 9.3891, df/dx1 = 18.7781, df/dx2 = 8.3891; Adam t=2 step 0.9178 eta, uncorrected 3.162 and 3.900; cross-entropy 3.065884, exp overflows at 710). e2(b) is also checked against autograd to 1e-17.
